answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with identity maturation: a new identity starts near the reef, its votes and attestations worth almost nothing, and only gains weight as it survives epoch after epoch of honest, verifiable work. Like an island rising slowly toward its zenith, trust accrues gradually and resets to zero on any proven misbehavior. An attacker must therefore maintain thousands of fake identities for many epochs, doing real useful work the whole time, so the cost of the attack approaches the cost of being a genuine participant, which destroys the Sybil advantage.
